In the event of a crash, the database can be recovered from the write-ahead log, which is a record of all the changes that were written to the database but not yet committed. The write-ahead log is essentially a list of operations that were supposed to be performed on the database, but were not completed before the crash.
When the database is restarted, it can use the write-ahead log to replay all the operations that were in progress when the crash occurred. This means that the database can be restored to a consistent state, as if the crash had not happened. The write-ahead log acts as a backup of the database's state at the time of the crash, allowing the database to recover its data and resume normal operation.
The write-ahead log is not a traditional backup in the sense that it is not a snapshot of the database's state at a particular point in time. Instead, it is a record of the changes that were made to the database, which can be used to recreate the database's state after a crash. This approach has several advantages, including faster recovery times and the ability to recover from crashes that occur during complex operations.
